headline: Advance Daily Access Passes for St. Lawrence Islands
reservation: Entry requires a daily access pass which should be purchased online in advance through the SEPAQ portal as park capacity is strictly limited. Note that camping reservations at the Grosbois campground are managed separately and do not automatically guarantee vehicle entry if day-use limits are reached. Systems may transition to mandatory pre-booking seasonally, so verify the current status on the official website.

days.title: St. Lawrence River Discovery

stops.name: Île Sainte-Marguerite
stops.detail: Visit the park's main hub to access the nautical center and explore the wetlands via the multi-use trail system.

stops.name: La Grande Coulée
stops.detail: Traverse the channel views between islands where herons and white-tailed deer are frequently observed in the marshland.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from downtown Montreal; conditions vary with bridge traffic
days.note: The park is accessible by car via the Louis-Hippolyte Lafontaine Tunnel or seasonally by river shuttle.

days.title: Historic Grosbois and River Channels
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from the Visitor Center

stops.name: Île de la Commune
stops.detail: Walk the loop through open fields and observe the unique agricultural history still visible in the island landscape.

stops.name: Le Chenal-du-Moine
stops.detail: Paddle the calm, protected waters of the channel to see the park from a water-level perspective away from the bike paths.

days.driving: Internal travel via bicycle or walking; vehicles restricted to main lots
days.note: Rentals for canoes and kayaks are seasonal and availability depends on river conditions.

days.title: Wetland Ecology and Observation

stops.name: Île aux Raisins
stops.detail: Explore the smaller footpaths that highlight the biodiversity of the archipelago's forested sections.

stops.name: Grosbois Archaeological Site
stops.detail: Visit the eastern end of the park to learn about the First Nations presence and early settler history in the region.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from local Boucherville gateways; bridge construction may impact timing
days.note: Expect higher pedestrian and cyclist volume on weekends due to proximity to the urban core.

intel.title: River Shuttle Logistics
intel.text: Seasonal water taxis operate from Montreal and Longueuil directly to the islands. Check the Navettes Fluviales schedule as these services are independent of park entry fees.

intel.title: Seasonal Wildlife Closures
intel.text: Certain trail sections may be restricted during the spring thaw or deer management periods. Consult the visitor center maps upon arrival for the most current zone accessibility.

intel.title: Main Entrance Constraints
intel.text: The primary parking area is located on Île Sainte-Marguerite and often reaches capacity early on summer weekends. Consider using the overflow lots near the Boucherville side if the main gate is restricted.

intel.title: Urban Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally strong throughout the archipelago due to proximity to Montreal. Digital maps are reliable, but paper brochures at the entrance are helpful for specific channel navigation.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: No fuel or grocery services are available within the park boundaries. Complete all provisioning in Boucherville or Longueuil before crossing the bridge or boarding the ferry.

plan.arrival: Pick up rentals at YUL airport, proceed through the Louis-Hippolyte Lafontaine Tunnel, and stop in Boucherville for supplies before entering the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are ideal; large RVs may find the tunnel and internal park parking lanes narrow.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the western shore of Île Sainte-Marguerite, offering views of the Montreal skyline across the St. Lawrence.
